subject: PHI handling boundaries, BAA availability & deployment options — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@medilogix.com>
Cc: MediLogix Procurement <procurement@medilogix.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: PHI handling boundaries, BAA availability & deployment options — next steps

Hi Alex — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

Call notes (short):
- Primary use case: document summarization and entity extraction from clinical intake forms (PHI includes name, DOB, MRN, limited clinical notes).
- Ingest pattern: batch uploads (SFTP) with occasional low-latency lookups.
- Required contractual ask: BAA, and clarification on which deployment modes are eligible for PHI.
- Compliance evidence: MediLogix requested SOC 2 background and to kick off the vendor security questionnaire.

Redwood answers / immediate items:
1) BAA: Redwood can sign a standard BAA for customers handling PHI. I attached a draft (BAA_Draft_v0.3.docx) for your review — it reflects our typical terms and can be edited.
2) Deployment modes for PHI: We support three tiers — Hosted API (hosted by Redwood), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools), and Private (VPC or on-prem). For PHI:
   - Hosted API: allowed for customers who accept our default data handling controls and retention settings; recommended only if you do not require customer-managed networking or HSM-backed keys.
   - Dedicated: generally acceptable for PHI when combined with a signed BAA and customer isolation; provides stronger data separation and predictable throughput.
   - Private (VPC/on-prem): the preferred option for regulated workloads with strict network or key management requirements.
3) SOC 2: See attached SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf — short summary of our controls. Full Type II report will be available under NDA; we can initiate that exchange once procurement confirms.
4) Next steps (proposed):
   a) You: confirm the PHI elements you expect to send (sample fields) and whether the SFTP flow will include files > PII only or full clinical notes.
   b) Redwood: send the BAA draft (attached), updated deployment matrix (attached) and a short security questionnaire template for your team to complete.
   c) Schedule a 30-min follow-up with our solutions architect to review network/topology constraints (suggested times in the Doc below).

I attached the deployment matrix that maps PHI-level to recommended hosting mode. If procurement wants legal edits to the BAA we can loop in our legal counsel.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: BAA_Draft_v0.3.docx (draft), Deployment_Matrix.xlsx (xlsx), SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@medilogix.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: MediLogix Procurement <procurement@medilogix.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling boundaries, BAA availability & deployment options — next steps

Thanks Sean — really helpful summary. A few quick clarifying items from our side before we move the BAA into legal review:

1) PHI scope: we will be sending names, DOB, MRN, and short clinician notes (up to ~1,200 chars). No imaging, no raw DICOM.
2) Retention: we cannot accept long-term storage on Redwood side beyond 90 days for any original intake documents; derived vectors/embeddings are okay if obfuscated. Can you confirm retention windows and whether customer-controlled deletion APIs exist?
3) Keys: we prefer customer-managed keys (KMS) or HSM for production; is this supported on Dedicated/Private options?
4) SOC 2: procurement asks if the Type II report is already available or only forthcoming; also request an inventory of any subservice organizations.

Procurement also asked for a short security questionnaire before we send the final SOW. Can you send the one-page questionnaire and preferred timeline for SOC2 NDA exchange? We are targeting an internal decision by 05/20.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Brenner | Head of Product, MediLogix
alex.brenner@medilogix.com | +1 (617) 555-9876

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@medilogix.com>
Cc: MediLogix Procurement <procurement@medilogix.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 5 May 2027 08:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling boundaries, BAA availability & deployment options — next steps

Alex — thanks, all good notes. Quick answers inline then next steps: 

- Retention: default hosted retention for original files is 30 days. We offer configurable retention windows up to 90 days for customers with a BAA; we also provide a delete endpoint to purge customer data and can schedule a one-time purge on contract start. Ive noted the 90-day requirement.
- Keys: customer-managed KMS/HSM is supported on Dedicated and Private deployments; Hosted API supports envelope encryption with customer-managed keys in some regions (well confirm availability for your region).
- SOC 2: we are completing SOC 2 Type II for the inference platform with an expected report availability by end of Q3 2027. The SOC2_Summary_v2.pdf attached lists subservice orgs (cloud provider, CDN, and managed DB vendor). Full Type II report will be shared under NDA.

Attached: Ive uploaded a short 12-question security questionnaire (inline below) and re-attached the BAA draft + deployment matrix. If procurement can send back the completed questionnaire it will speed the SOC2 NDA and report exchange.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: procurement completes the questionnaire (well accept it in email or via our secure portal).
- 05/07: our security team issues an NDA link for SOC2 report access once questionnaire is received.
- 05/10-05/14: solutions architect deep-dive to confirm topology; pick a 30-min slot (I can coordinate).
- 05/20: target internal decision at MediLogix (per your note).

Would you like me to route the BAA draft directly to your legal contact or do you prefer to review internally first?

Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com

Attachments: Security_Questionnaire_12q.pdf (pdf), BAA_Draft_v0.3.docx (docx), Deployment_Matrix.xlsx

From: MediLogix Procurement <procurement@medilogix.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Alex Brenner <alex.brenner@medilogix.com>
Date: Thu, 6 May 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: PHI handling boundaries, BAA availability & deployment options — next steps

Sean / Alex — procurement here. We reviewed the materials; a few practical items before legal review: 

1) Please confirm whether the Hosted API option can be configured to purge originals at 0 days (i.e., process in-memory only) for tokenization and then drop — this would be our preferred approach for PII minimization if possible.
2) For the Dedicated option: wed like a short diagram showing network egress paths and whether VPC peering is required. A one-page topology would be ideal.
3) We will fill out the 12-question security questionnaire and return by EOD 05/04 (note: they meant 05/07 per timeline) — after that please send the NDA link for SOC 2 report access.

If you can confirm (1) and (2) in writing well loop legal. Thanks!

Procurement Team
MediLogix
procurement@medilogix.com
